title: OpenAI's AI is Building Itself: The Automated Intern is Here!
summary: OpenAI has officially reached its goal of creating an automated research intern to accelerate its own R&D processes. The company aims to develop a fully automated AI researcher by March 2028, with current AI agents already drastically outpacing human labor metrics.
raw_text: So check this out, guys, OpenAI just dropped a massive report on September 6th about how their own AI is literally building better AI. Honestly, this is huge. They officially announced they've already hit their milestone for an 'automated research intern' and are making strong progress toward a fully automated AI researcher by March 2028. I mean, we always knew AI would help code, but we are looking at 3.1 agent-workdays of effort logged for every single human workday as of mid-August. Think about that insane scale! You've got an AI army practically doing the heavy lifting in the background. Their engineers are heavily relying on these coding assistants now, completely transforming their R&D workflows. They did mention they are rolling this out carefully with incremental tests and safety safeguards, which is reassuring, but the sheer speed here is what completely blows my mind. Are human researchers going to be obsolete in two years? Drop your thoughts in the comments!

title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2: Humanoid Robots Are Taking Over
summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2, a new suite of models designed specifically to control humanoid robots. These models allow robots to plan complex tasks, execute full-body movements, cooperate in teams, and operate offline.
raw_text: Here's the wild part of today's tech news—Google DeepMind just announced Gemini Robotics 2, and it brings us one massive step closer to a sci-fi reality. This is a brand new family of models built specifically to control humanoid robots. We aren't just talking about a robotic arm picking up a block anymore; these models allow robots to plan out complex tasks, execute full-body movements, and even cooperate with each other in teams. DeepMind revealed a model called 'ER 2' for complex planning, and another called 'On-Device 2' that runs completely offline directly on the robot. They also rolled out a brand new safety benchmark for testing how these robots behave around humans, which is definitely needed. With government interest in robotics and Tesla pushing Optimus, Google is throwing down the gauntlet here. I genuinely believe these AI models are going to put real, working robots in manufacturing and logistics much sooner than we thought. What do you guys think?

title: Tesla Cybercab LAUNCHED! No Steering Wheel, No Pedals!
summary: Tesla debuted its fully driverless, two-seat Cybercab robotaxi in Austin, Texas on September 3, 2026, which lacks a steering wheel and pedals entirely. The day after the launch, U.S. regulators launched an inquiry into the vehicle's self-certification, highlighting ongoing regulatory hurdles for autonomous vehicles.
raw_text: Alright guys, Tesla just changed the game again. On September 3rd, they officially launched their fully driverless robotaxi, the Cybercab, right in Austin, Texas. Get this—it's gold-colored, seats two, and has absolutely zero steering wheel or pedals. It was built from the ground up purely for autonomous driving. Passengers in Austin can literally hail one right now using the Tesla app, and Elon Musk says he expects an absolute 'storm' of these on the streets. But here's the catch: the very next day, U.S. federal regulators opened an inquiry into how Tesla self-certified this thing as safe without manual controls. Tesla is arguing that the old rules just don't apply since a human isn't meant to drive it. This is a massive real-world test for next-gen autonomous vehicles that could drastically cut ride costs and improve mobility, but the government is clearly keeping a close watch. I want to know, would you feel safe riding in a car with no steering wheel?

title: NVIDIA Buys Hugging Face for $13 BILLION?!
summary: On September 3, 2026, NVIDIA announced its intent to acquire the leading open AI model repository, Hugging Face, for $12.93 billion. While NVIDIA pledges to keep the platform multi-cloud and hardware-agnostic, the deal has sparked industry concerns regarding potential neutrality issues and bias against NVIDIA's competitors.
raw_text: I literally could not believe my eyes when I saw this. On September 3rd, NVIDIA casually announced they are buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion!. Yes, billion with a B. Hugging Face is the absolute holy grail for open AI, hosting over 3 million models, half a million datasets, and a million AI apps. It is used by millions of developers worldwide. NVIDIA claims the deal, which closes in early 2027, won't ruin anything—they promised to keep the platform multi-cloud and hardware-agnostic, swearing they won't force users onto NVIDIA GPUs. But let's be real, industry analysts are freaking out. Having NVIDIA own the central hub of AI raises massive neutrality concerns. Will the platform secretly favor NVIDIA over AMD or Google TPU?. This cements NVIDIA as the undisputed king of AI infrastructure, but the open-source community is definitely nervous. Are you worried about NVIDIA's monopoly? Sound off in the comments!

title: UK Launches £100M 'Sovereign AI' Fund to Fight US & China
summary: The UK government initiated a £100 million Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme on September 1 to fund domestic AI startups solving public-service challenges. The initiative aims to position the UK as a leader in AI by leveraging government purchasing power while allowing participating companies to retain their intellectual property.
raw_text: Let's take a quick look at the global policy side of AI. On September 1st, the UK government launched a massive £100 million competition called the Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme. They are basically pouring cash into domestic AI startups to tackle major public-service challenges like NHS productivity, national security, and cyber-resilience. Chancellor John Healey and AI Minister Kanishka Narayan are pushing this hard, wanting to make sure the UK takes a lead role in AI globally instead of just relying on the US and China. What's actually pretty cool for founders is that participating companies get to keep their IP to commercialize it beyond just the UK government. Experts are looking at this as a massive test of 'sovereign AI' strategy. If this works and actually stimulates local tech growth and jobs, we might see governments all over Europe copying this exact playbook.

title: OpenAI BANS Cursor After Elon Musk Buys It!
summary: Following SpaceX's acquisition of Anysphere, the parent company of the AI coding assistant Cursor, OpenAI announced it will terminate API support for the tool by November 12, 2026. OpenAI cited terms-of-service concerns based on past violations by Elon Musk-owned companies, forcing Cursor developers to urgently seek alternative models.
raw_text: The drama never stops! OpenAI just announced they are completely cutting off API support for Cursor, the super popular AI coding assistant. Why? Because SpaceX—yes, Elon Musk's company—just acquired Cursor's parent company, Anysphere. OpenAI sent them a notice in early September saying they are pulling the plug on model access effective November 12, 2026. OpenAI is officially blaming 'terms-of-service concerns,' pointing out that Musk's other companies like X and xAI have violated their terms in the past. This is absolutely brutal for anyone relying on Cursor for their daily coding workflow. It proves how incredibly fragile the AI supply chain really is—your favorite tool can lose its brain overnight just because of a billionaire corporate feud. Cursor teams are now scrambling to migrate to Anthropic or open-source alternatives before the shutdown. Do you guys use Cursor? What are you switching to?
